scale.3: Fully satisfactory. Completeness: all task requirements met. Quality: correct, appropriately presented, free of misleading content.
scale.2: Mostly satisfactory. Completeness: at least 75% of the task requirements met. Quality: only minor deficiencies that do not affect the main conclusions.
scale.1: Partially satisfactory. Completeness: only part of the task addressed or essential requirements omitted. Quality: substantive errors (incorrect data or masking, conclusions inconsistent with the reference results or the reported numerical values).
scale.0: Unsatisfactory. Completeness: no valid output or output unrelated to the task. Quality: fundamentally incorrect or no evaluable result.

rules.completeness: Checked against every explicit item in the query's 'Expected visualizations' (panels, order, layout, shared scales, centring, units/labels, overlays, annotations).
rules.quality: Correctness of the plotted fields, masks, coordinates and depth/time axes, and clarity of presentation. 3 = correct and clear; 2 = minor presentation defects that do not change the reading (overlapping colourbars/titles, legends or annotations covering data, axis limits that clip a small part of the data, a series hidden under another, truncated bar baseline, global maps cropped at high latitudes, grid-gap stripes from a display-only regrid, an arbitrary-sign mode drawn with inconsistent signs across panels); 1 = wrong data, masking or projection, or a misleading display (including stripes or holes from a broken regrid that also defines the comparison sample behind the reported metrics, a curvilinear field drawn as if it were regular, unmasked land counted as ocean, and a colour scale set by a few outliers so that the field itself cannot be read); 0 = no figure.
rules.not_graded: Numerical accuracy of the plotted values (graded separately) and stylistic choices the query leaves open (colormap, map projection, colour-limit percentile).
rules.repeats: Every completed run is scored on its own. In folders with repeats, per_task[T] is a list with one entry per scored run (repeat 1 = the first run of each task); summary means are the mean over tasks of the per-task mean over runs. Runs still in progress when the file was written are listed under not_scored.
